::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** March 25th 1865  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS British Library Add MSS 54920: 71-72
:::

My dear [Mr Macmillan](people/person_939.qmd),
This is a quick fire upon a busy man, but there are two or three things to say, and first that [Mme de Witt](people/person_423.qmd) has written to say that the [Christian Names](cmy_books/cmybook_48.qmd) have not reached her, and asking whether you have sent them through any Paris <u>bibliothèque</u> where they could be enquired for. I also enclose a direction to which I should like to send a copy of the [Golden Deeds](cmy_books/cmybook_51.qmd). It is in fact to the little Princess [Marguérite](people/person_956.qmd) of Savoy, a child of 13, the niece of Victor Emmanuel - but it is etiquette to give it to the [Governess](people/person_1931.qmd) instead of herself. She has been writing a poem on the Gascon Squire in the [Lances of Lynwood](cmy_books/cmybook_23.qmd)! 

If I did not know about her and the governess through [Miss Sewell](people/person_1301.qmd) and some friends of hers I should think it a hoax, as I really did the first proposal to translate a book of mine which came on April 1st

Here is the 1st chapter of [Bethlehem](organizations/other_177.qmd). I have had a young friend here, and so have been hindered from going further. I think there is scope for a very beautiful illustration here. In the latter part I could take no words but the Bible and Milton.

'The Debatable Ford' would be as suitable a title as the [Dove](cmy_books/cmybook_62.qmd) &c and perhaps might be the first. I believe my [brother](people/person_1624.qmd) would say the Dove &c was 'flummery' - but most I have told of it have liked the sound of it, and it tells the story. The length seems to me its chief fault. I had better leave the decision between the Dove and the Debatable Ford to you and [Professor Masson](people/person_980.qmd).

Do you know if there is a publisher named [Ratcliffe](people/person_1933.qmd) at Calcutta -? About three years ago the [Calcutta University](organizations/other_175.qmd) [bought](organizations/other_160.qmd) of me an edition of 5000 of my [Landmarks /of Ancient History](cmy_books/cmybook_14.qmd)\\ for their schools &c and two days ago, I got a letter dated Kyd Street, Calcutta, signed Ratcliffe, and saying the University had published another edition and that he was going to pay me 3d per vol. Whether it is a banking or a publishing firm or a government office, I cannot make out - there is not even the initial of a Christian name.

I’m afraid my Scotch was not rightly original for I wrote the sense in pencil, and sent it to a friend in Edinburgh to translate into good Scotch, or it never would have had such genuine turns.[^1] 

I know how great a friend [Mrs Gatty](people/person_549.qmd) considers [Mr Bell](people/person_1930.qmd), and I should hardly have mentioned her, but for her having translated that '[Bit of Bread](other_books/otherbook_354.qmd)' by special request, I believe, for [Messrs Saunders and Otley](organizations/other_144.qmd), so that I concluded there was some understanding about her taking individual bits of work for individual purposes. But of course I would say nothing to her. I should like to see a very choice volume on Creation, and the book of nature, if one could only find a person with the head and the heart and the perseverance all united as in [Dr George Wilson](people/person_1932.qmd) or [Hugh Millar](people/person_1813.qmd).[^2]

Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: In fact the letter was from James Sutcliffe, principal of the Hindu College, Calcutta.
[^2]: In *The Clever Woman of the Family*. The “friend” was probably [Anne Mackenzie](people/person_930.qmd), (1813-1877), with whom CMY had stayed in Edinburgh in July 1862.
[^3]: *Macmillan's Magazine* I (1860) 199-203 had carried an obituary by John Cairns of the chemist, museum director and popular science writer George Wilson (1818-1859).
